content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The slice is an axial view of a limb, likely the lower leg. The bright heterogeneous mass sits in the posterior-central region, around x=400, y=450 in the left panel. In the right panel the same area is at about x=1180–1240, y=420–480.

Checking the marks near that region:
- Mark 516 is at (1149, 489), which falls within the heterogeneous bright mass.
- Mark 541 is at (1098, 394), which is above the mass and in the intermuscular region.
- Mark 494 is at (1229, 416), which is at the dark rim near the bone or fibula-like structure.

The mass spans roughly x=335–465 and y=400–510 in the left panel, which is x=1120–1250 in the right panel. Mark 516 at x=1149, y=489 is inside the mass, in its lower left part. The mass centre is around (1190, 455), so 516 is the closest option that is clearly inside the tumor.

ANSWER: 516
